pharm: Inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis, producing anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic effects.

May take with food or antacids to reduce GI upset

Avoid in advanced renal disease; risk of renal toxicity

summary: Oxaprozin is a long-acting propionic acid NSAID used for the symptomatic treatment of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. Its long half-life permits once-daily dosing. Like all NSAIDs it carries boxed warnings for increased risk of serious cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious gastrointestinal bleeding/ulceration. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration. It is contraindicated in the setting of CABG surgery and in patients with aspirin/NSAID-induced asthma or urticaria. Photosensitivity reactions can occur.
indications: Relief of signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis
Relief of signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis

dosage.n: Lowest effective dose; lower starting dose (600 mg) for low body weight or milder disease

dosage.d: Up to 1800 mg/day (or 26 mg/kg, whichever is lower) given in divided doses
dosage.n: Maximum dose; reserve for those needing additional benefit
For low body weight, milder disease, or risk factors for GI/renal events

admin: Take once daily; may divide doses above 1200 mg/day
Take with food, milk, or antacids if GI upset occurs
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Caplets may be split/halved where a product permits to give 600 mg
Advise sun protection due to risk of photosensitivity
moa: Oxaprozin nonselectively inhibits the cyclooxygenase enzymes COX-1 and COX-2, blocking the conversion of arachidonic acid to prostaglandins and thromboxanes. Reduced prostaglandin synthesis at sites of inflammation produces anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic effects. Inhibition of constitutive COX-1-derived prostaglandins underlies gastrointestinal and renal adverse effects, while effects on platelet thromboxane and prostacyclin balance contribute to cardiovascular risk.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reaction after aspirin or other NSAIDs
Treatment of perioperative pain in the setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
relative: Active peptic ulcer disease or GI bleeding
Significant renal impairment or risk factors for renal injury
Heart failure, hypertension, or established cardiovascular disease
Third trimester of pregnancy / from 20 weeks gestation

preg: Avoid NSAIDs at about 20 weeks of gestation and later because of risk of fetal renal dysfunction leading to oligohydramnios; use at 30 weeks and beyond is contraindicated due to risk of premature closure of the ductus arteriosus. If use between 20-30 weeks is necessary, limit to the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
lact: It is not known whether oxaprozin is excreted in human milk in clinically significant amounts. Because of potential serious adverse effects in the infant, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or the drug; avoidance is preferred.
renal: NSAIDs reduce renal prostaglandin synthesis and can precipitate renal decompensation, especially in volume depletion, heart failure, hepatic dysfunction, or with concurrent diuretics/ACE inhibitors/ARBs. Avoid in advanced renal disease; monitor renal function and correct volume status before and during therapy.
hepatic: Borderline elevations of liver tests may occur; rarely severe hepatic reactions including jaundice and fatal hepatitis have been reported with NSAIDs. Monitor for signs of hepatotoxicity and discontinue if liver disease develops or systemic manifestations occur. Use caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Anticoagulants (e.g., warfarin) - increased risk of serious GI bleeding
Aspirin - increased GI toxicity with little added benefit; antiplatelet effect of low-dose aspirin may be blunted
Other NSAIDs / corticosteroids - additive GI ulceration and bleeding risk
moderate: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and diuretics - reduced antihypertensive effect and increased risk of acute renal failure (triple whammy)
Lithium - reduced renal clearance, increased lithium levels
minor: Histamine H2 antagonists/antacids - minimal effect on absorption
interactions.food: May be taken with food or antacids to limit GI upset; food may slightly delay absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it increases the risk of gastrointestinal ulceration and bleeding.
interactions.diagnostics: May cause false-positive urine benzodiazepine immunoassay results; can alter renal function and liver tests.

monitoring: GI symptoms and signs of bleeding
counsel: Take once a day, ideally with food to protect your stomach
Stop and seek care for black/tarry stools, vomiting blood, severe stomach pain, chest pain, or weakness on one side
Avoid alcohol and avoid taking other NSAIDs or aspirin unless your doctor advises
Use sunscreen and protective clothing as this medicine can make your skin sensitive to sunlight
Tell your doctor about heart, kidney, liver, or stomach problems and any blood thinners you take
pk: Analgesic effect within a few hours; full anti-inflammatory effect over days
Effect spans 24 hours with once-daily dosing
Store at controlled room temperature; protect from moisture
pearls: Very long half-life (~40-50 h) enables once-daily dosing but means slow accumulation and slow washout
Carries NSAID class boxed warnings for cardiovascular thrombotic and GI bleeding risk - use lowest dose, shortest time
Contraindicated for peri-CABG pain and in aspirin/NSAID-sensitive asthma (Samter triad)
Notable for causing photosensitivity - counsel on sun protection
Can cause false-positive urine benzodiazepine immunoassays
missed: If you miss your once-daily dose, take it when you remember on the same day. If it is almost time for the next day's dose, skip the missed dose. Never take two doses to make up for a missed one.
overdose: Symptoms may include lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain, usually reversible with supportive care; serious effects (GI bleeding, hypertension, acute renal failure, respiratory depression, coma, seizures) can occur. Management is supportive: empty the stomach if recent and large ingestion, give activated charcoal, monitor and treat symptomatically. Hemodialysis is not useful (high protein binding).
